title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning Jurisdiction and Scope of Application of Law in the Trial of Trademark Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 2 The first-instance cases listed in item 1 of Article 1 of this Interpretation shall be under the jurisdiction of the relevant intermediate people's courts within the jurisdiction of the Beijing Higher People's Court as determined by the Beijing Higher People's Court pursuant to the authorization of the Supreme People's Court.
The first-instance cases listed in item 2 of Article 1 of this Interpretation shall have their jurisdiction determined in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law.
First-instance trademark civil dispute cases shall be under the jurisdiction of intermediate people's courts or above.
Each Higher People's Court may, in light of the actual circumstances of its jurisdiction and with the approval of the Supreme People's Court, designate one or two primary people's courts in relatively large cities to accept first-instance trademark civil dispute cases.

Article 3 Where a trademark registrant or an interested party requests the National Intellectual Property Administration to handle an act of infringement of trademark rights, and also brings an action in the People's Court for infringement of trademark rights and claims damages, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 4 Where the National Intellectual Property Administration accepts a case before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, and makes a review decision or adjudication after the said Decision comes into force, if a party is dissatisfied with the review decision or adjudication and prosecutes before the People's Court, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 5 Except as otherwise provided in this Interpretation, with respect to administrative cases where the circumstances concerned occur before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force and fall within the situations enumerated in Article 4, Article 5, Article 8, paragraph 1 of Article 9, items (2), (3), and (4) of paragraph 1 of Article 10, paragraph 2 of Article 10, Article 11, Article 12, Article 13, Article 15, Article 16, Article 24, Article 25, and Article 31 of the amended Trademark Law, and the National Intellectual Property Administration makes a review decision or adjudication after the Decision comes into force, if a party is dissatisfied and prosecutes before the People's Court, the corresponding provisions of the amended Trademark Law shall apply for review; if they fall under other situations, the corresponding provisions of the pre-amendment Trademark Law shall apply for review.

Article 6 Where a party has a dispute over a registered trademark that has been registered for one year or more at the time when the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, and is dissatisfied with the adjudication made by the National Intellectual Property Administration and prosecutes before the People's Court, the time limit for filing an application provided in paragraph 2 of Article 27 of the pre-amendment Trademark Law shall apply; where the trademark registration is less than one year at the time when the Decision comes into force, the time limit for filing an application provided in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 41 of the amended Trademark Law shall apply.

Article 7 For an act of infringement of the exclusive right to use a trademark that occurred before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, if a trademark registrant or an interested party, after the Decision comes into force, applies to the People's Court before prosecution for the adoption of measures ordering cessation of the infringing act or preserving evidence, the provisions of Articles 57 and 58 of the amended Trademark Law shall apply.

Article 8 For a case prosecuted for an act of infringement of the exclusive right to use a trademark that occurred before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, if the People's Court has not yet rendered a legally effective judgment at the time when the Decision comes into force, the case shall be handled with reference to the provisions of Article 56 of the amended Trademark Law.

Article 9 Except as otherwise provided in this Interpretation, for a trademark civil dispute case accepted by the People's Court after the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, if the civil acts involved occurred before the Decision comes into force, the provisions of the pre-amendment Trademark Law shall apply; if the civil acts involved occurred after the Decision comes into force, the provisions of the amended Trademark Law shall apply; if the civil acts involved occurred before the Decision comes into force and continued to the period after the Decision comes into force, the provisions of the pre-amendment and amended Trademark Law shall apply respectively.

Article 10 Where a case of trademark infringement dispute accepted by the People's Court has already been handled by an administrative department, the People's Court shall still examine the facts of the civil dispute between the parties.
